correctness.rationale: For real scalar Lipschitz seminorms on a unit-edge depth-two m-by-k tree, averaging any right inverse under S_k^m semidirect S_m is contractive and fixes leaf values; all symmetric candidates reduce to root mu0 and branch alpha*mu_i+(1-alpha)*mu0. The exact dual norm of any zero-mass signed leaf measure is sum of absolute leaf masses plus sum of absolute branch masses, by tree-edge telescoping with attaining sign potentials. Root-branch edge norm is 4(m-1)|alpha|/m. A concrete leaf test potential gives the affine branch-leaf lower bound 4-2(k+1)(1+(m-1)alpha)/(mk). Their minimax intersection alpha* lies strictly between 0 and 1; in that range direct dual norm computes attainment on every edge. Hence Lambda=4(2mk-k-1)/(m(3k+1)) globally over ALL linear operators. Algebra gives >2 iff (m-2)(k-1)>4 and monotone limiting supremum 8/3. Independently computed 1,936 exact edge dual norms across all 64 pairs (2<=m,k<=9), confirming but not replacing the minimax proof.

originality.rationale: Fefferman–Klartag proves existence of bounded W^{1,p}, 1<p<infty, extensions on binary trees with weighted bulk energy; this is distinct from sharp Lipschitz p=infty for every homogeneous depth-two branching pair. Bruè–Di Marino–Stra supplies general random-projection-based Lipschitz extension operators with bounds rather than a sharp exact finite-tree constant. Resultary one-point star and p-Banach formulas apply to different extension geometries and cannot simply be substituted. Best-of-knowledge specific exact norm appears new, with finite-tree literature priority risk.
